Build the body that writes an outcome back into the register

outcome_payload.Rd

The register holds two kinds of field and they must never mix. What a person asked for is intent; what happened is observation. This body carries only the second, and the columns are fixed here rather than assembled from the caller so that a bug cannot rewrite intent: without that separation a repeated transport error could switch off legitimate requests, and nobody could tell "a person removed it" from "a bug removed it".

Usage

outcome_payload(record_id, outcome, detail = "", at = "", applied_as = "")

Arguments

record_id

The register record to write to.

outcome

One of "pending", "applied", "data_error", "transport_error", "simulated".

detail

Error codes or a human-readable note.

at

When the outcome was recorded, as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM.

applied_as

What the re-read found.

Value

A one-row data frame with exactly the outcome columns.

Details

applied_as is meant to carry what the channel read back after writing, not the return code. An outcome that only said "no error" would be the same thing as the four spike cases that reported true while doing something else.
